Induced Smoothed Lasso

📦 Installation

You can install the development version of islasso from GitHub:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("gianluca-sottile/islasso")

Once installed, load the package:

library(islasso)

🔍 Description

islasso implements the Induced Smoothed Lasso (Cilluffo et al., 2020): the non-smooth lasso (or elastic-net) penalty is replaced by its expectation under the approximate sampling distribution of the estimator, so that standard errors (sandwich formula), Wald tests, confidence intervals and general linear hypotheses are available for all the coefficients.

Key features:

  • numerical core in C (BLAS/LAPACK): majorise–minimise or Newton iterations on a smooth convex objective, only the diagonal of the sandwich during the iterations, Woodbury identities when p > 2n (cost O(n^2 p) instead of O(p^3));
  • any GLM family and link accepted by glm() (binomial with logit/probit/cloglog/cauchit/log, Poisson, Gamma, inverse Gaussian, quasi families, negative binomial, …);
  • regularisation paths with warm starts and tuning-parameter selection by cross-validation or information criteria (AIC, BIC, AICc, eBIC, GCV, GIC);
  • relaxed fits, general linear hypotheses, diagnostic plots (ggplot2).

🚀 Quick Example 

sim <- simulXy(n = 100, p = 50, beta = c(rep(1, 5), rep(0, 45)), seed = 1)
mod <- islasso(y ~ ., data = sim$data, control = is.control(seed = 1))  # lambda by 5-fold CV
summary(mod, pval = 0.05)
confint(mod, parm = 2:6)

path <- islasso.path(y ~ ., data = sim$data, nlambda = 50)
GoF.islasso.path(path)$lambda.min
